clue.text: Remarked on fortified wine in a Mediterranean city

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on (after) another puts it to the right

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from the Douro
remarked means said

explanation.surface: Someone passes comment on the local fortified wine while visiting a Mediterranean city.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Said is an Egyptian city at the Mediterranean end of the Suez Canal.

clue.text: Family in fix in old Beijing

indicators.note: one piece placed in another signals that the family word sits inside the fix word

parts.note: to fix something is to peg it
kin means family

explanation.surface: A family finds itself in a fix in the old Chinese capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Peking is the older romanised name for the Chinese capital now spelt Beijing.

clue.text: Piece that is for a beginner

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A chess piece suitable for someone just learning the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer or novice, especially a first-year recruit.

clue.text: Film part, an opening

parts.note: a stage is a part or phase of a process
a door is an opening in a wall

explanation.surface: A scene from a movie showing an entrance or gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film part' looks like one phrase, but 'Film' alone is the definition: Stage Door is a 1937 Hollywood film.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage Door is a 1937 film starring Katharine Hepburn and Ginger Rogers, named for a theatre's back entrance.

clue.text: Not legislating, curiously, for swag

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so these letters are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A lawmaker oddly declines to pass laws about stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for loot, money or goods obtained dishonestly.

clue.text: Close to Edinburgh, soldier's after a good Scottish dish

indicators.note: the soldier's piece comes after the preceding letters
the close of a word is its final letter, so only the end of Edinburgh is used

parts.note: taken as written
GI is an American soldier, and GI'S gives GIS

explanation.surface: Near Edinburgh, a soldier goes in search of a good traditional Scottish meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis, a savoury pudding of sheep's offal and oatmeal, is Scotland's national dish.

clue.text: Detached, a goose soaring

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, soaring means the goose word rises, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a goose is a silly person, a fool

explanation.surface: A goose flies high above, remote from everything below.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof describes someone distant, reserved and uninvolved.

clue.text: A couple of drinks ahead of my card game

indicators.note: the drinks come ahead of, before, the word my

parts.note: gin is one spirit
rum is the second spirit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has two drinks before settling down to play cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin rummy is a two-player card game, a variant of rummy.

clue.text: Worker after strong cloth, one with stripes

indicators.note: the worker comes after the cloth in the answer

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled fabric
a worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A labourer comes after durable fabric, someone wearing striped garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant wears chevron stripes on the sleeve to show rank.

clue.text: One testifying unexpectedly? Suspect wishes to listen

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means doubtful or dodgy, signalling these letters are unsound and rearranged

explanation.surface: A suspicious person in court wants to hear what is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostile witness is one whose courtroom testimony turns against the side that called them, hence the question mark.

clue.text: At the moment everyone is following king, a wise guy

indicators.note: the other pieces follow the king letter

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
at the moment means now
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A courtier now follows the king about, posing as a clever adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is someone who behaves as if they know everything; wise guy is ironic.

clue.text: Croon on broadcast with singer Sinead

indicators.note: broadcast can mean scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An Irish singer croons on a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinead O'Connor was an Irish singer known for Nothing Compares 2 U.

clue.text: Lacking judgment? Cut out time in local!

indicators.note: cut out means remove, so the time letter is taken away

parts.note: a local person is a native

explanation.surface: Someone foolish enough to skip drinking time at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' suggests a British pub, but here it means a native of a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means unsophisticated and credulous, short on worldly judgment.

clue.text: Rarely at home, a Parisienne, discordant?

parts.note: someone rarely at home is often out, so out plus oft
une is French for a, as a Parisian woman would say it

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman rarely at home who perhaps sings off-key.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of tune means sounding discordant, not at correct pitch.

clue.text: Servant holding collection for old railway worker

indicators.note: holding means the servant word wraps round the collection word

parts.note: a footman is a liveried household servant
a collection in church is taken on a plate

explanation.surface: A butler carries the church offering for a retired railwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: A footplateman was a locomotive driver or fireman, working on a steam engine's platform.

clue.text: Course artist announced for planner

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: a tack is a sailing course and Titian a Venetian painter, together said tack-Titian

explanation.surface: An art course is advertised for someone who likes to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: TACK is a sailing boat's course; Titian is the Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactician is someone skilled at planning moves to reach a goal.

clue.text: Tending to obstruct elected one's false claim

parts.note: a politician elected is in
I is the Roman numeral one; 's means has

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so these letters are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A newly elected politician makes a false claim that blocks progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means hostile or harmful, working against something.

clue.text: Ballet's second week, an excess?

parts.note: taken as written
a lake is a surplus, as in a wine lake

explanation.surface: Asking whether a ballet's second week of performances is overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAKE is a large stored surplus, as in the European 'wine lake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's famous classical ballet.

clue.text: NB young bishop has to proceed quickly to small Scottish town

parts.note: new means young or fresh
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to run is to proceed quickly
Wick is a town in Caithness, far northern Scotland

explanation.surface: A young bishop must hurry to a small town in Scotland: note well.
explanation.walkthrough: NB looks like 'nota bene', but it is the postal abbreviation of the Canadian province.
explanation.definitionFit: NB is the official abbreviation for the Canadian province on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Improvement in score for musical

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A musical's score gets better after revision.
explanation.definitionFit: A reform is a change for the better, an improvement.

clue.text: Quickly disposing of note causing emotional tension

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of, so the note is removed

parts.note: Mistress Quickly is the hostess in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Rushing to throw away a memo is a sign of nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quickly' reads as an adverb, but it is Shakespeare's tavern hostess, Mistress Quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental or emotional strain caused by pressure.

clue.text: Beggar declaring inability to rehabilitate?

parts.note: to rehabilitate is to restore or mend
one declares inability by saying I can't

explanation.surface: A beggar explains he cannot reform himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads as the exchange 'Mend? I can't', with the pieces put in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is someone who lives by begging, such as a friar.

clue.text: Go with oil, unwisely, in house

indicators.note: unwisely means foolishly, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly takes oil heating into their home.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dome-shaped dwelling built of snow blocks.

clue.text: It holds back writer being cack-handed

indicators.note: holds means the It word contains the reversed writer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means the writer word is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Something restrains a clumsy author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cack-handed' is British slang for clumsy; 'It' looks like the subject but is letters taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, clumsy or incompetent.

clue.text: Old comedian securing place in series

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the series word encloses the place abbreviation

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked things
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A veteran comic secures a spot in a TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was a famous silent-film comedian of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Record one's poem for part of series

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
one is the letter I; with 's it gives I'S
an ode is a lyrical poem

explanation.surface: Someone records their poem for one instalment of a broadcast series.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single instalment of a serial or series.

clue.text: Go to ground, small one the Spanish filled

indicators.note: filled means the small word has the other pieces put inside it

parts.note: low means small, as in low in height
I is the Roman numeral one
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A small Spaniard digs in, keeping out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is to hide away and avoid notice.

clue.text: Destructive waves must, as in novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A novel must feature destructive waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are huge sea waves usually caused by undersea earthquakes.
